clue.text: Did it show the way to Mafeking?

definitions.text: Did it show the way to Mafeking?

parts.words: Did it show the way to Mafeking?
parts.note: plays on the Relief of Mafeking, the 1900 lifting of a siege in the Boer War, as if 'relief' were the kind of map showing hills and valleys

explanation.surface: A historical question about which chart guided travellers to the South African town of Mafeking.
explanation.walkthrough: The Relief of Mafeking (1900) was a famous British moment in the Boer War; the clue pretends a map named after that relief showed the route.
explanation.definitionFit: A map showing land contours is called this, and the clue's question puns on the siege's lifting.

definitions.meaning: to collect funds or troops, as in levying an army
an increase, as in a pay rise

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are plain synonyms: levying funds or troops is collecting them, and an increase in price or pay is the noun sense.

clue.text: Jumps high in a supple way, perhaps

indicators.note: 'in a supple way, perhaps' suggests the letters bend into another shape, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone springs upward with lithe, flexible agility.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring upward with a bound is to make a high jump, a plain phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Put your name down to go in

definitions.meaning: to sign up for a competition
to come into a room or place

explanation.definitionFit: Signing up for a race is one sense of the verb, and coming into a room is its everyday sense.

parts.note: pitch here is tar, the sticky black binder, not a slope or a sports field

explanation.surface: A phrase that seems to describe the slope or camber of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarred broken-stone road surfacing, named after the engineer John McAdam, is bound with pitch.

clue.text: Chopin piece of sole piano variation

indicators.note: a musical variation reworks a theme, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A Chopin work arranged as a variation for solo piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote many of these stately Polish dances for piano, so it is an example of his pieces.

definitions.meaning: lines of seats or soldiers set side by side

explanation.surface: Arguments breaking out among the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisy quarrels are one sense of the noun, and lines of people or seats side by side are the other.

clue.text: After several appearances, new trio perform without restraint

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a run is a series of performances of a show

indicators.note: something new is made fresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Following a series of shows, a newly formed trio plays with wild abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave wildly and out of control is the idiom's meaning, a fair match for acting unrestrained.

clue.text: Going crazy with a wine list may eventually affect this

definitions.text: Going crazy with a wine list may eventually affect this

indicators.note: letters that go crazy are thrown into disorder and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Overindulging from the restaurant's wine menu will in time show on your figure.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: drinking too freely from a wine list eventually expands the measurement around your middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy drinking adds weight around the middle, so the girth measurement is what suffers.

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a gig is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage
an antic is a playful caper or prank

explanation.surface: A wonderful romp aboard a horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something huge or enormous, a straight synonym.

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Asking what an Italian eats while fasting, or perhaps his heartbeat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible seeds of legumes such as peas and beans, and this small lens-shaped seed is one.

definitions.meaning: someone who teases or ribs others playfully

explanation.definitionFit: A brain-twister is one sense, and a person who teases playfully is the other, both formed from the verb tease.

parts.note: a bridge here is a dental fitting spanning missing teeth, not a structure over a river

explanation.surface: People who seem to be engineers spanning gulfs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tooth doctors fit bridges, false teeth anchored across a gap where teeth are missing.

definitions.meaning: to conclude or round off a matter

explanation.definitionFit: To conclude a meeting is one sense of this phrasal verb, and British slang uses it to mean shut up.

clue.text: Manage to get a game of golf by artful deception

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a round is one complete game of golf

explanation.surface: Arranging a golf outing through a crafty trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given evasive treatment and misleading excuses is the idiom's meaning, so it is deceit.

clue.text: Petty formality that may turn out to be unpolitic

indicators.note: letters that turn out to be something else are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: Fussy etiquette that can prove tactless.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine point of etiquette or a fussy detail of conduct is exactly a minor formality.

definitions.meaning: to keep something up or provide for it

explanation.surface: A demand that the government should provide financial help.
explanation.definitionFit: Three plain verb synonyms: to assert firmly, to declare, and to keep up or provide for someone.

clue.text: Recent furore about an actor's appearance

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the next piece
a furore is an uproar, so these letters are thrown into turmoil

explanation.surface: A recent uproar over an actor coming on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'furore' looks like the uproar in the story, but it scrambles RECENT into ENTRCE, and 'about' wraps that round AN.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor coming on stage makes this, the theatrical term for appearing in a scene.

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of place and come out rearranged

explanation.surface: Creatures that snorted on being woken.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats, mice and squirrels are gnawing mammals, so these are a kind of animal.

clue.text: Head left students to get good jobs

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, has gone away

explanation.surface: A headteacher has departed so pupils can find decent work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head left' looks like a leader quitting; it says the first letter of LEARNERS leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nice little earner is a lucrative job, so these are good jobs.

clue.text: Happened to go to law, in extremity

indicators.note: the legal piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone resorted to legal action as a last resort.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow as a result is to occur afterwards, a synonym of took place.

parts.note: boarders here ride boards on the waves, not lodgers at a seaside guesthouse

explanation.surface: A pastime for guests staying at a seaside boarding house.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding waves on a board is the sport of people with boards at the beach.

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Referring to the crocodile's famously insincere tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Crocodile tears are false sympathy; the surface leans on that idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile hunts and kills other animals, so it is an example of a hunter.

parts.note: the tenor of a speech is its drift or gist

explanation.surface: A singer is at present unable to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating without control at the mercy of the current means being lost and powerless.

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

explanation.surface: A northern district that contains a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium or enclosed space for contests is exactly a sports venue.

parts.note: a serviceman here is a tennis server, not a soldier

explanation.surface: Asking about an error committed by someone in the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an invalid serve is called by this name, so it is the server's error.

parts.note: a passage dug beneath the ground, not a line on the London Underground

explanation.surface: A line on the London Tube network.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage bored beneath the earth or a hill is a route below ground.

clue.text: Retired female retained worth as an honorary professor

indicators.note: the first piece keeps the second inside it
retired means drawn back, so the name reads backwards

explanation.surface: A retired woman kept her value as a professor with an honorary title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' suggests the professor's status but it turns SUE backwards into EUS, and 'retained' sets MERIT inside those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A professor who has retired keeps this title as an honour, so it fits an honorary academic.

indicators.note: text that needs editing will be reworked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some verse really requires an editor's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a form of verse, so a set of them is some poetry.

clue.text: Random laughs not seen as offensive

indicators.note: random letters are in no set order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stray chuckles that are regarded as rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A military offensive is a fierce attack, the same as a violent assault.
